source.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
source.authors: Alan Baade; Kyle Sargent; Vincent Sitzmann; Eric Ryan Chan; Justin Johnson; Fei-Fei Li; Gordon Wetzstein

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to visual tokenizer encoders, measuring how image-generation diffusability varies with encoder training scale. It does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports image-generation FID/FD scaling with visual encoder compute, not language-model loss. The compute-budget comparison evaluates tokenizer-plus-generator generation quality, not the parameter/token allocation trend in V3. Table 1 ablations and the FID-50K comparison in Table 3 do not measure a scaling law and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of image-generation quality (FID-10K on ImageNet, FD-DINOv2-10K on GPIC) against RePR tokenizer-encoder training compute, across about two orders of magnitude. That is a new setting (image representation learning) for the power-law form in V5. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss of the encoder. The quality metric is that of a downstream generator trained on the encoder's features, so this is a proxy for loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RePR encoders show scaling laws for diffusability on ImageNet and GPIC, with generation improving predictably with encoder compute. They also conclude that RePR plus Latent Forcing beats direct pixel diffusion (JiT-L) at matched total training FLOPs, making representation learning an added scaling axis.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales visual representation encoders and measures image-generation FID/FD, rather than scaling language models and measuring held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the width-1024 ImageNet encoder begins to overfit after 200 epochs, while scaling continues beyond that regime on GPIC. The sweep uses width-only scaling with depth held fixed.
record.problems: The scaling evidence uses visual diffusability metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss. The text gives no uncertainty estimates or fitted exponents for the trends, and the extrapolations are limited to at most 1× beyond the measured log-scale FLOP range.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported encoder-scaling points in Tables 7 and 8 were left out. Other generation comparisons and ablations were omitted because they do not measure a scaling trend or the fixed-compute parameter/token allocation in the claim.

untested.parts: The encoder's own pretraining loss versus compute; video; repeated data; fine-tuning and transfer; depth scaling.
Fitted laws are extrapolated to predict the compute needed for DINOv2- and WebSSL-level quality, but no large run checks the predictions.
No parameter/token optima are fitted against compute. The tokenizer-vs-generator FLOP split in Fig. 4/Table 3 is a different allocation question.
Width-only scaling with fixed depth; no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Language-model downstream tasks, and the link between pretraining loss and downstream performance.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Fitted power-law predictions: DINOv2-level ImageNet FID at 1.504e21 FLOPs (1/7.77 of DINOv2 compute). WebSSL-level GPIC FD at 1.229e21 FLOPs (1/7.96). Extrapolation is at most 1x beyond the measured log range and not verified.
missing.locator: Appendix A.7, text below Table 8; Section 6.2

missing.what: Overfitting of the width-1024 ImageNet encoder after 200 epochs, stated in text only

record.verdict_notes: Claims about the fit (exponents, goodness of fit) are made without reported exponents or uncertainty. The GPIC baseline FD (MiniT2i 546.3) and the DINOv2 and WebSSL references are comparison points, not rows. The V6 links were removed because the versions are framed around language models; the image-domain downstream result is recorded under V5.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of language-model loss on runs orders of magnitude larger than the fitted runs.
The study compares image-generation quality at compute budgets but does not fit parameter-count and token-count optima as powers of compute, or compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann trends.
The encoder sweep changes width while holding depth fixed; it does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The study tests image tokenizer-encoder scaling using generation diffusability metrics, not the same held-out pretraining-loss measure as the language-model claim. It does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
It evaluates image-generation quality from image encoders, not language-model downstream tasks or the relationship between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance.
The study does not compare language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, and does not report a systematic fit-dependence analysis.

rows.subject: RePR encoder scaling sweep
rows.operation_detail: Scale RePR encoder training compute and evaluate generation diffusability.

conditions.value: roughly two orders of magnitude of training compute

rows.measure: Image-generation FID-10K versus encoder training compute
rows.value: Consistent power-law scaling across roughly two orders of magnitude of training compute.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; the paper does not give fitted exponents here.
rows.check: Drop V6. V6 concerns downstream predictability of language models; this image-domain result belongs under V5. Measure is downstream FID of a fixed JiT-B generator, not encoder loss. No exponents are given in the text.

relationships.reason: Authors report consistent power-law scaling of generation quality with encoder compute over about 2 orders of magnitude (r1, r2). Table values fall monotonically with size and epochs (r3–r50). The metric is downstream FID/FD, not held-out loss.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream FID/FD improves with reported power-law compute scaling over about two orders of magnitude and decreases monotonically with model size and training epochs.

relationships.condition: ImageNet, width-1024 encoder beyond ~200 epochs; smallest 20M encoder at long training
relationships.reason: Text says the width-1024 ImageNet model begins to overfit after 200 epochs, so the trend holds only within a data-limited regime. The 20M encoder plateaus (r5 37.01 to r6 37.21). The overfitting claim is text-only; the table stops at 211 epochs (r20).
relationships.display_finding: The width-1024 encoder began overfitting after about 200 epochs, while the 20M encoder plateaued with values changing from 37.01 to 37.21.
